coverage.target: monitoring-design.md Metrics & KPIs — the grant-request p95 has a source (Identity `support_write_duration_seconds`, surface-wide, no route label) but not a route-labelled one; infrastructure-specification.md Deployment keeps `identity-api` at 3 × 0.5 CPU / 512 MB and `gateway` at 2 × 0.5 / 512, so a single attempt never waits on a sizing decision. The one-attempt rule itself is a console suite assertion, not an infrastructure choice

The 15 s `deadlineMs` and `DeadlineError` are client transport (nfr-design performance §2). No infrastructure decision exists to make: the gateway's `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS: 2000` and the service timeouts are unchanged by this unit (infrastructure-specification.md Services)

monitoring-design.md states the own-grant read p95 as an **unmeasured target** with no series at all — a route-labelled histogram is not this unit's to add — while infrastructure-specification.md fixes what is measurable: one read from `support_access_grants` under Identity's own role with `MY_GRANTS_LIMIT = 20`, needing a `(support_agent_id, requested_at DESC)` index that the S2 delivery ships as an up/down migration pair because the shipped indexes (one leading on `user_id`, one partial on the live pair) cannot serve it; no sizing change

monitoring-design.md — Identity `support_read_duration_seconds` (surface-wide) bounds the metadata read; infrastructure-specification.md Services records that `identity-api` already carries `ACCOUNT_URL`/`PORTFOLIO_URL`/`AUDIT_URL` for the fan-out and needs no change, and that U3's 500 ms fan-out budget is not this unit's

The 30-second tick and the expiry timeout are client-side timers (nfr-design performance §6). No scheduled job, queue or server timer is introduced; infrastructure-specification.md confirms no new container or background worker

Sign-in reuses Supabase Auth through the shell (`src/auth/session.ts`); infrastructure-specification.md Services keeps Supabase Auth unchanged and the unit adds no auth call, no refresh loop and no external origin
`retry: false` is query-client policy set in the console hooks (nfr-design performance §3). No retry, backoff or idempotency behaviour changes at any infrastructure hop
Rendering `ApiError.retryAfterSeconds` is client code. The limiter and its `Retry-After` header are existing gateway behaviour, unchanged here (infrastructure-specification.md Services, gateway row)
`refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `refetchInterval: false` are console query options (nfr-design performance §3). Nothing infrastructure-side issues or suppresses a request

monitoring-design.md Logs & tracing (audit bullet) and infrastructure-specification.md Storage — the projection lives only in the in-memory query cache, the static host is `read_only: true` with tmpfs, and a route-level 403 drops the key, so nothing survives an access-ended answer on disk or in a browser store

The filter narrows already-returned rows in component state (nfr-design performance §5); it issues no request and has no server or infrastructure counterpart. The 20-row bound is enforced by Identity, recorded in infrastructure-specification.md Supabase Postgres row

infrastructure-specification.md Deployment — egress: no new browser-external origin, the pre-existing Google Fonts load is unchanged, and the console CSP in `web/nginx.conf` (`connect-src 'self' https://*.supabase.co`) is untouched; every U9 data call is a same-origin `/v1` path behind the TLS edge

infrastructure-specification.md Shared Infrastructure, edge access logs — nginx logs the request URL only, never a body or a credential-bearing header; the reason travels in the `POST /v1/support-grants` body, S2's path is static, and S3's grant-UUID path is recorded as an accepted residual. The three places that still name the retired `X-Support-Reason` header are corrected in the same change: `support-console/README.md:29,33`, `web/nginx.conf:7-9`, `services/gateway/infrastructure/src/upstream.rs:88-90`

infrastructure-specification.md Storage / Infrastructure Services (`web` nginx row) — `read_only: true` with tmpfs for nginx scratch, `index.html` `no-store`, hashed assets immutable; the unit adds no volume, no storage API and no browser persistence, so nothing it holds can outlive the session

infrastructure-specification.md Infrastructure Services — the gateway forwards the user's Supabase JWT unchanged and every service validates it against JWKS on every route; the console's role read decides only what is offered, and this unit adds no token handling or infrastructure for it

infrastructure-specification.md Shared Infrastructure, gateway `/v1` route table — deny-by-default and first-match, so an undeclared path is `404` before a service is reached; S1 and S3 are existing entries; S2 is declared by no open change, which is the release blocker, and no browser path reaches a service directly

infrastructure-specification.md Shared Infrastructure, gateway route table — a `Route` is `method`, `pattern`, `service`, `requires_admin` and `max_requests_per_minute` with no role field beyond the boolean, so the gateway cannot enforce the support role and the refusal is Identity's on every path; a client that ignores its own role gate is refused server-side and, on a route-level 403, the console clears only its `["support", …]` keys

infrastructure-specification.md Storage — the grant, reason draft, filter and projection are memory-only and discarded on access end; no volume, no cache tier and no server-side session store is added

infrastructure-specification.md Infrastructure Services, gateway row — S1 (`POST /v1/support-grants`) is 20/min and S3 (`GET /v1/support-grants/{grantId}/metadata`) 60/min at `services/gateway/domain/src/route.rs:154` and `:158-160`; S2 has **no** per-route budget and rides the shared per-caller-address budget, stated as such rather than invented, with a per-route limit left as an optional addition to the route by the change that declares it

infrastructure-specification.md gateway row states the honest bound — `check_route` is in-process and per replica, so a 2-replica gateway allows up to twice a per-token budget; monitoring-design.md records that a limiter `429` is counted only in the gateway's 4xx status class (record_metrics is the outermost layer), with no route label and no 429-specific series

The projection's field whitelist is client and Identity code (nfr-design security §5). No infrastructure surface carries the excluded classes: the console adds no route, no store and no origin through which they could travel
`pickSupportMetadata`'s whitelist and throw-on-malformed behaviour are pure client functions (nfr-design security §5); there is no infrastructure decision in a client-side picker

infrastructure-specification.md Shared Infrastructure edge logs plus Security note — the reason is body-only, never pre-filled, echoed, or placed in a URL, header, log or telemetry event; the header path is retired and its three stale references are corrected in this unit's change

Error rendering (status plus correlation id, never `ProblemDetails.detail`) is client code. The `x-correlation-id` header itself is an existing gateway behaviour recorded in monitoring-design.md Logs & tracing, unchanged by this unit

React's default escaping is a rendering concern; the console ships no new origin, template engine or `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` path (infrastructure-specification.md egress row — nothing external is added)

monitoring-design.md Logs & tracing, audit bullet — this unit writes and reads no audit record and provisions no audit infrastructure; the create and the metadata read are audited by Identity (U3, C9), and the console renders only the statement that the read is recorded, so a `403` never claims an audit that did not happen

infrastructure-specification.md Infrastructure Services, Supabase Postgres row — no table change and no migration from this unit; S2 reads the existing `support_access_grants` table under Identity's own role and DSN, needs a `(support_agent_id, requested_at DESC)` index that the S2 delivery ships as an up/down pair (the shipped `support_grants_read_idx` leads on `user_id` and `support_grants_live_pair_idx` is partial), and is not delivered by any open change
The four-status model and the absence of a `denied` producer are client and contract facts (nfr-design security §7); no store, enum or infrastructure component encodes a status

The clock-derived status, the fail-closed treatment of a missing `expiresAt`, and the server's 403 as access ended are client behaviour (nfr-design security §7, performance §6). Nothing infrastructure-side evaluates grant status

infrastructure-specification.md Shared Infrastructure, gateway route table — every client-side gate is presentational and every U9 route is re-authorised server-side in Identity; a tampered client receives 403 from a real service behind the deny-by-default table, not from an edge rule this unit would have to configure

Role and status come from the signed token and the server's answers at request time (nfr-design security §7); the 60-minute window is computed by Identity. No infrastructure component reads or caches either

Accessible landmarks, table captions and keyboard operation are component concerns (nfr-design security §8). No infrastructure decision exists; the design adds no overlay, iframe or third-party widget that would change that
Live regions, field labels and `aria-invalid` wiring are client component work (nfr-design security §8); nothing at the edge or in the services participates
`StatusBadge` and the Parchment Ledger presentation mapping are frontend design-system work (nfr-design security §8); no infrastructure surface renders status
Keyboard operation and reading order are component concerns (nfr-design security §8); no infrastructure decision

cicd-pipeline.md stage 7 — `yarn --cwd support-console test` is a blocking gate running Vitest with jest-axe over the MSW handlers, so every rendered state's axe assertion is enforced at build time; a state without one is a review-time defect
`Intl.DateTimeFormat` output for `expiresAt` and `lastSyncedAt` is client formatting (nfr-design security §9); no infrastructure component formats or emits a timestamp to the person

infrastructure-specification.md What must exist — a console-wide localisation unit (no owner unit exists yet; tracked as decision `ab46b27b`); the console has no i18n module, and this unit neither adds one nor forks a second mechanism. Recorded as deferred, not met
`Intl` degrading to its default rather than an empty date is client behaviour (nfr-design security §9); no infrastructure or locale configuration is introduced
